profile.title: Tensor Apprentice

quest.objective: Implement an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) to fuse noisy GNSS and IMU telemetry.
quest.brief: Build an EKF pipeline in C++ or Python that ingests synthetic sensor streams and tracks vehicle 6-DOF position and velocity under non-linear motion models.
steps: Derive the non-linear motion and observation Jacobians for bicycle vehicle kinematics.
Implement prediction and correction update loops handling out-of-order and dropped packets.
Benchmark state estimation error metrics against synthetic ground truth trajectories.
quest.tangibleDeliverable: A tested C++ state estimation package with synthetic sensor data generation and evaluation plots.

rubric.name: Filter Convergence
rubric.description: Estimator covariance converges within 20 timesteps without divergence during turns.

rubric.name: Latency Profile
rubric.description: Per-step update latency executes below 5 milliseconds on sample synthetic streams.

rubric.name: Covariance Consistency
rubric.description: Normalized Estimation Error Squared (NEES) remains within 95% chi-square bounds.

curatedResources.title: Kalman and Bayesian Filters in Python

interviewQuestions: How do you detect and handle filter divergence caused by unmodeled sensor biases?
What are the computational trade-offs between an Extended Kalman Filter and an Unscented Kalman Filter?

quest.objective: Formulate and execute a Model Predictive Controller (MPC) for high-speed lateral control.
quest.brief: Develop a non-linear MPC using CasADi or OSQP that tracks high-curvature trajectories while respecting actuator saturation constraints.
steps: Formulate kinematic and dynamic bicycle models with tire friction constraints.
Set up the quadratic programming optimization problem with slack variables for slip angles.
Simulate trajectory tracking against dynamic disturbances such as variable friction surfaces.
quest.tangibleDeliverable: MPC implementation repository with automated trajectory tracking visualizations and tuning scripts.

rubric.name: Tracking Accuracy
rubric.description: Cross-track error remains below 0.15 meters at speeds up to 15 m/s.

rubric.name: Constraint Enforcement
rubric.description: Steering angle rate and tire slip limits are strictly respected without solver failures.

rubric.name: Solver Determinism
rubric.description: MPC optimization solves within the 20 millisecond control cycle limit.

interviewQuestions: How do you formulate slack variables in MPC to prevent infeasibility during sudden disturbances?
What are the core differences between Kinematic and Dynamic bicycle models in real-world control?

nodes.title: Trajectory Generation & Motion Planning
nodes.subtitle: Search-based planning & Frenet frame trajectory generation

quest.objective: Develop a real-time Frenet frame local trajectory planner for dynamic obstacle avoidance.
quest.brief: Create a lattice trajectory generator that transforms global waypoints into curvilinear coordinates, generates candidate maneuvers, and evaluates collision costs.
steps: Transform global cartesian road maps into curvilinear Frenet s-d coordinates.
Generate longitudinal and lateral quartic and quintic polynomial trajectories.
Score trajectories using jerk, curvature, distance-to-obstacle, and lane-centering cost functions.
quest.tangibleDeliverable: C++ trajectory planner repository benchmarked against dynamic obstacles in simulated highway environments.

rubric.name: Collision Avoidance

rubric.name: Comfort & Feasibility

curatedResources.title: Optimal Trajectory Generation for Dynamic Street Scenarios - Werling et al.

interviewQuestions: What are the advantages of planning in the Frenet frame compared to Cartesian space?
How do you mathematically bound lateral acceleration and jerk during high-speed lane changes?

quest.objective: Construct a 3D LiDAR odometry and mapping module backed by factor graph optimization.

steps: Implement point cloud voxel filtering, ground plane removal, and normal estimation.
Construct frame-to-frame scan matching using G-ICP to generate odometry factors.
Integrate loop-closure verification and optimize the global pose graph with GTSAM.

messages.text: Welcome to Ascendra! I reviewed your starting profile for the AI Research Engineer path. The reverse-mode autodiff project is an excellent foundation. When you start the custom PyTorch CUDA ops quest, make sure you pay close attention to memory pinning and gradcheck numerical stability.
Hi Dr. Vance, can you review my approach to KV-cache optimization?

I'd be glad to take a look! For an aspiring Autonomous Systems Engineer, mastering KV-cache efficiency is critical—onboard compute for autonomous platforms doesn't give you the luxury of endless H100 clusters. You are dealing with strict real-time latency budgets, thermal throttling, and hard VRAM ceilings where tail latency (P99) can dictate safety. 

Before you drop the code or architecture spec, I want to know where your optimization is targeted. Are you tackling the *runtime/memory management* layer—say, non-contiguous block allocation similar to vLLM's PagedAttention, chunked prefill, or low-bit quantization (FP8/INT4 scales)—or are you working on *algorithmic eviction*, like StreamingLLM with attention sinks, heavy-hitter eviction, or cross-layer sharing? For autonomous agents running long horizon-planning loops, how you preserve critical temporal tokens versus transient sensor noise makes or breaks your context window.

Drop your implementation details, pseudocode, or PyTorch snippet along with how you're profiling it. Make sure you include your baseline metrics: are you measuring TTFT (Time-to-First-Token), inter-token latency (ITL), or pure memory fragmentation via PyTorch’s CUDA memory snapshot or Nsight Systems? Let's see what you've built.
